2	name: gravity-ui
3	description: Builds, fixes, styles, and composes UI with the Gravity UI design system — the React ecosystem of @gravity-ui/* packages (uikit, charts, table, navigation, date-components, icons, and more). Routes to the correct package when look-alikes exist, applies theming and required setup, and prevents invented component APIs. Applies when working with @gravity-ui imports, uikit, ThemeProvider, --g- CSS tokens, or any prompt (EN or RU) mentioning gravity-ui, гравити, дизайн-система, компоненты, дашборд, таблица, график, or форма. Also installs required specialized Gravity UI packages when they are absent.
4	---
5	
6	# Building UI with Gravity UI
7	
8	Build UI on **real** Gravity UI components, not from memory. Gravity UI is a
9	multi-package React design system (`@gravity-ui/*`), so the two things that go
10	wrong are picking the wrong package and using an API from the wrong version.
11	This skill routes you to the right package, grounds you in the installed
12	version, and stops you from inventing APIs — match the installed versions and
13	follow the ecosystem catalog instead of guessing.
14	
15	## Efficiency guardrails
16	
17	- Do not read the same file twice. Reuse evidence already present in the session.
18	- Do not dump a reference file wholesale. Use targeted `rg -n -C 4` searches and keep each result below
19	  200 lines unless the whole file is necessary to resolve the task.
20	- Batch package, component, and symbol lookups into as few commands as possible.
21	- Stop documentation research as soon as package choice, import path, required setup, and uncertain props
22	  are confirmed. Documentation is evidence for decisions, not a checklist to read in full.
23	- Do not query unpkg, package source repositories, or alternative documentation mirrors.
24	- Do not install browsers or screenshot tooling, and do not start a dev server for routine verification,
25	  unless the user explicitly requests visual or browser verification.
26	- Run typecheck/build after implementation. If it fails, inspect only the failing API, fix it, and rerun
27	  the check. Do not repeatedly rebuild unchanged code.
28	
29	## Step 0 — pick the right package first (ecosystem routing)
30	
31	Before doing anything else, work out which `@gravity-ui/*` library the task
32	needs. Do not guess from training data — the ecosystem has look-alike packages
33	(`charts` vs `chartkit`, uikit `Table` vs `@gravity-ui/table`, `date-components`
34	vs `date-utils`, …) and picking the wrong one is the #1 failure.
35	Choose from the task's functionality, not only from dependencies already present in the project.
36	Open [`references/package-routing.md`](references/package-routing.md) and read
37	its top **first**: it opens with a task → package decision table that settles the
38	common cases (landing page, dashboard, data grid, calendar, charts, editor, app
39	shell, i18n), followed by the ecosystem catalog with a one-line "what it's for /
40	what to use instead" per package for everything else. Use it to choose the
41	package, then come back here for Step 1.
42	
43	Search the catalog for the task's relevant terms and read the matching package entries. Do not read the
44	entire catalog when its top and those entries are sufficient.
45	
46	Only after the package is chosen, run Step 1 to ground in that package's
47	installed version and API.
48	
49	## Step 1 — ground in the installed version of the chosen package
50	
51	1. **Read `package.json`.** Note each installed `@gravity-ui/*` package and its
52	   version. The installed version is the source of truth, not your memory.
53	   Resolve ranges from `node_modules` (`<pkg>/package.json` `version` field), not
54	   the range string in the root `package.json`.
55	
56	   If the chosen specialized package other than `@gravity-ui/uikit` is absent, add it with the project's
57	   existing package manager before importing it. Install its documented peer dependencies too, then
58	   resolve the installed version and continue with the local evidence below. Do not fall back to uikit,
59	   raw HTML, or a foreign library merely because the specialized package was initially absent. If
60	   installation is blocked, report the exact failure.
61	
62	2. **Fetch the docs for the package you are about to use, in this order,
63	   stopping at the first source that answers your question:**
64	
65	   (a) **LOCAL** — start with `node_modules/@gravity-ui/<pkg>/dist/docs/INDEX.md` or `node_modules/@gravity-ui/<pkg>/build/docs/INDEX.md`.
66	      If `INDEX.md` is absent for this package, fall back to the package's root `node_modules/@gravity-ui/<pkg>/README.md`.
67	      This is the *exact* installed version — always preferred for version-sensitive questions.
68	      Note: bundled docs are a recent addition — `uikit` ships `build/docs` only from **7.45.0**;
69	      older installs have no local docs at all, and that is expected, not an error. Go to (b).
70	      If an import, component, hook, or prop remains uncertain, inspect only its exact installed `.d.ts`
71	      before moving online. Batch all uncertain symbol lookups for that package.
72	   (b) **ONLINE** — per-package llms.txt at the **major line**:
73	      `https://gravity-ui.com/llms/<pkg>/<major>/llms.txt`
74	      (e.g. `/llms/uikit/7/llms.txt` for `^7.2.1`). The major-line URL serves the
75	      latest minor of that major — it tracks the major but not the exact patch.
76	      Use it when LOCAL has no docs for the package.
77	
78	3. **Fallback rule — never silently proceed on a failed or empty source:**
79	
80	   - If LOCAL has no README / `dist/docs` / `build/docs` for the package, or they are empty
81	     → fetch the ONLINE major-line llms.txt (b).
82	   - If the ONLINE request fails — network timeout, DNS, connection refused
83	     (air-gapped / corporate proxy), HTTP 404 (major not hosted), or an empty /
84	     non-markdown body → fall back to LOCAL README + dist/docs or build/docs (a).
85	   - **Do NOT use the `/llms/<pkg>/llms.txt` "latest" alias** as a fallback — it
86	     serves the newest major, which may differ from the installed one and have a
87	     different API. The major-line URL is the versioned fallback; below it, go
88	     LOCAL, not "latest".
89	   - If BOTH are unreachable for a package → STOP and tell the user the
90	     package's docs are unreachable. Do not guess its API from training data.
91	
92	For a bounded local inspection, run:
93	
94	```sh
95	.agents/skills/gravity-ui/scripts/inspect-package.sh uikit Button Card Switch ThemeProvider
96	```
97	
98	The script reports the resolved version, available local documentation, and declaration files matching
99	the requested symbols. Read only the returned files needed to confirm an uncertain API.
100	
101	## Step 2 — implement on the chosen packages, then typecheck
102	
103	1. **Implement using only the `@gravity-ui/*` packages chosen in Step 0 and
104	   confirmed installed in Step 1.** Import from those packages exactly — do
105	   not substitute look-alike libraries (MUI, Ant, plain `<input>`) and do not
106	   reach for a `@gravity-ui/*` package that Step 1 did not confirm installed.
107	   Follow the prop APIs from the docs you just read, not memory; if a prop
108	   you want is not documented, it does not exist — use the documented one, or
109	   ask the user.
110	
111	2. **Apply the cross-cutting rules** in `rules/hallucination-traps.md` while
112	   writing: typography variants, the flex contract, theming/ladders,
113	   `Button view`, `Icon data`. Per-component traps live in the package's own
114	   `dist/docs`.
115	
116	3. **Typecheck before declaring done.** Run the project's typecheck command
117	   (typically `tsc --noEmit`; for monorepos, the workspace's typecheck script).
118	   Fix every error before reporting completion — a type error almost always
119	   means a wrong/invented prop, a wrong import path, or a version mismatch,
120	   which is precisely what Steps 0–1 were meant to prevent.
121	
122	   - If the typecheck surfaces a prop/path that contradicts the docs you read
123	     in Step 1, trust the **installed version** (the typechecker), not the
124	     docs snapshot — the docs may be from a different minor. Re-ground: read
125	     the package's `dist/docs/INDEX.md` in `node_modules` for the exact
126	     installed types.
127	   - If the typecheck is unavailable (no TS in the project), say so
128	     explicitly and ask the user how they want to verify; do not silently
129	     skip verification.
130	   - **Escape hatch.** If the user explicitly waived verification ("just
131	     sketch it", "quick prototype", "no need to check"), you may skip the
132	     typecheck — but state this plainly in your reply: *"typecheck skipped by
133	     user request — code is not verified"*. Do not skip silently.
134	   - **Know what typecheck does not cover.** A green `tsc` proves the API is
135	     real; it says nothing about layout or contrast. Before reporting done,
136	     say so, and either check or list for the user to check by hand: the
137	     screen in both `light` and `dark` themes (text and controls on colored
138	     fills especially), narrow (~375px) and wide (~1400px) viewports for
139	     horizontal overflow, and empty / loading / error states.
140	
141	## Hard rules
142	
143	- **`@gravity-ui/uikit` MUST be installed in every Gravity UI project.** It is
144	  the base component + design-token library every other `@gravity-ui/*` package
145	  builds on; without it components render unstyled. If `package.json` lacks it,
146	  stop and have the user install and configure it first (setup:
147	  `https://gravity-ui.com/llms/uikit/llms.txt`).
148	- **Read `package.json` before importing any `@gravity-ui/*` package.** Never
149	  assume a package is installed; never assume its major version.
150	- **Do not invent props or components.** Before using a component API you are
151	  not 100% sure of, check `rules/hallucination-traps.md` (ecosystem patterns)
152	  and the component's README in `dist/docs`. If still unsure, ask the user
153	  rather than guessing.
154	- **Never guess icon names** — they are hallucinated more often than not. To
155	  match an icon from a screenshot/photo/mock, run `scripts/icon-image-search.sh`
156	  (reverse image search). With only a description, look the name up on
157	  `gravity-ui.com/icons` or ask the user — do not invent one. Then pass it as an
158	  object (`<Icon data={CheckIcon} />`), never a string key. See
159	  `references/icons.md`.
160	- **Theming uses semantic `--g-*` tokens.** Never hardcode colors (`#fff`,
161	  `blue-500`); never hand-write `dark:` overrides. Full token tables live in
162	  `references/theming.md`; the cross-cutting traps (partial brand overrides,
163	  a `ThemeProvider` that themes the whole page, controls on a brand background) live in
164	  `rules/hallucination-traps.md`.
165	- **Required setup is package-specific** (style imports, `ThemeProvider`,
166	  peer-deps). It lives in each package's root README under "Required setup" —
167	  read it once per package, do not rely on memory.
168	
169	## What NOT to do
170	
171	These are the five most common ways agents break Gravity UI code. They are
172	already implied by the rules above; this section exists as an explicit
173	stop-sign. If you are about to do any of these, stop and re-ground.
174	
175	- **Do not substitute non-Gravity libraries.** No MUI, Ant Design, plain
176	  `<input>`/`<button>`, or look-alike component libs. Use the `@gravity-ui/*`
177	  package the task needs.
178	- **Do not invent component APIs or props.** If a prop is not in the docs you
179	  read in Step 1, it does not exist — do not write `variant=`, `color=`,
180	  `name=` (on `Icon`), or a `header-3` variant. Use the documented prop or
181	  ask the user. See `rules/hallucination-traps.md`.
182	- **Do not use the `/llms/<pkg>/llms.txt` "latest" alias as a fallback.** It
183	  serves the newest major, which may differ from the installed one and have a
184	  different API. The versioned online fallback is the major-line URL
185	  (`/llms/<pkg>/<major>/llms.txt`); below that, go LOCAL.
186	- **Do not partial-brand.** Setting only `--g-color-base-brand` leaves
187	  selection, focus, links and contrast on the default accent — a mismatched
188	  UI. Override the full brand token set, on each theme you support.
189	- **Do not override internal markup with `[class*='…']` / ID selectors.**
190	  That's written against one DOM structure and breaks silently when the
191	  component changes. Climb the customization ladder
192	  (global token → component CSS API → narrow flagged hack) before ever
193	  touching structure.
194	
195	## Deeper material — read on demand
196	
197	These files live alongside this SKILL.md and load only when relevant:
198	
199	- `references/package-routing.md` — offline snapshot of the ecosystem catalog
200	  (`gravity-ui.com/llms.txt`), refreshed each skill release. Used as the
201	  offline fallback in Step 0.
202	- `references/theming.md` — verbatim copy of uikit's `docs/theming.md`:
203	  `--g-*` token layers, `ThemeProvider`, branding, custom themes, scoped
204	  themes, `uikit-themer`. The bundled copy may lag — read
205	  `node_modules/@gravity-ui/uikit/build/docs/guides/theming.md` for the
206	  version-matched file.
207	- `references/layout.md` — verbatim copy of uikit's `docs/layout.md`:
208	  spacing scale (`--g-spacing-*`), `Flex`/`Box`, `Row`/`Col`/`Container`
209	  grid, breakpoints, `useLayoutContext`.
210	- `references/icons.md` — finding an icon by image
211	  (`scripts/icon-image-search.sh`) or on gravity-ui.com/icons; the
212	  object-vs-string rendering rule.
213	- `rules/hallucination-traps.md` — Incorrect/Correct pairs for the most
214	  commonly invented APIs: typography variants (`header-3..6` don't exist, no
215	  `Heading`), the flex contract (`min-width:0`, who shrinks), theming traps
216	  (partial brand overrides, a `ThemeProvider` that themes the whole page, customization
217	  ladder), `Button view` not `variant`, `Icon data` not `name`. Per-component
218	  traps live in each package's `dist/docs`, not here.

# Package routing — offline snapshot

This is an offline snapshot of **https://gravity-ui.com/llms.txt**, the Gravity UI
ecosystem catalog. It exists so Step 0 of the skill works when the online catalog
is unreachable (air-gapped, corporate proxy, timeout).

**Online is primary.** This snapshot may lag the site by one release — if you can
fetch `https://gravity-ui.com/llms.txt`, prefer it. Refresh this file at each
skill release by re-copying the catalog verbatim (generator = fetch the URL →
keep everything above the `---` line → write the file). Do not hand-edit the
catalog body below the line; edit the source `llms.txt` instead. The decision
table above the line is hand-maintained and survives the sync.

## Decision table — read this before the catalog

Settle the common tasks here; the catalog below is the reference for everything else (and it is long:
its decisive entries sit near the end, so do not skim its top and default to `uikit`).

| The task is… | Use | Not |
|---|---|---|
| A marketing / landing / promo page assembled from blocks (hero, features, CTA) | `@gravity-ui/page-constructor` (`PageConstructor` + `PageConstructorProvider`, block config) | hand-written sections from uikit primitives |
| A dashboard of freely arrangeable widgets | `@gravity-ui/dashkit` | a hand-rolled CSS grid, `react-grid-layout` |
| A table with sorting, checkbox selection, pagination | uikit `Table` + `withTableSorting` / `withTableSelection` + `Pagination` | `@gravity-ui/table` |
| A data grid that needs virtualization, column resizing / reordering, grouping, tree rows | `@gravity-ui/table` (TanStack-based) | uikit `Table` |
| A calendar, date / time / range picker | `@gravity-ui/date-components` (peer: `date-utils`) | a `Calendar` from uikit (does not exist), `react-datepicker` |
| Charts and data visualization | `@gravity-ui/charts` (`<Chart>`); `@gravity-ui/yagr` only for dense realtime series | `chartkit` (legacy wrapper), `recharts`, raw canvas |
| A Markdown / WYSIWYG editor | `@gravity-ui/markdown-editor` | `<textarea>` + custom preview |
| The app shell: aside navigation, header, footer | `@gravity-ui/navigation` (`AsideHeader`) | a hand-rolled `<aside>` |
| Interface language switching | uikit `configure({lang})` + `@gravity-ui/i18n` for app strings | `i18next`, `react-intl` |

Everything not listed — buttons, forms, dialogs, toasts, menus, tabs, theming — is `@gravity-ui/uikit`.
If the package from the table is not installed yet, **install it** with the project's package manager (and
its documented peer deps) — a project that only has `uikit` is not a reason to build the thing by hand.

---

# Gravity UI

Gravity UI is a open-source design system and ecosystem of React libraries for building web applications. This file is a compact catalog: pick a package, then fetch its per-package llms.txt for the full agent-facing docs. Read the user's `package.json` first and match the installed `@gravity-ui/*` versions — peer-version mismatches across the ecosystem are the most common failure.

> **`@gravity-ui/uikit` MUST be installed in every Gravity UI project.** It is the base component and design-token library that every other `@gravity-ui/*` package builds on — without it, components render unstyled. Check the user's `package.json` first.
>
> **If it is not installed, stop and have the user install and configure it before doing anything else.** Setup and theming instructions: https://gravity-ui.com/llms/uikit/llms.txt

> **Per-package docs are versioned.** Each package lives at `/llms/<package>/<version>/llms.txt` (exact version), `/llms/<package>/<major>/llms.txt` (latest of a major line), and `/llms/<package>/llms.txt` (latest). The links below point at `latest` — read the user's `package.json` and switch the URL to the installed version (or major) when it differs.

> **Agent skill recommended.** A `gravity-ui` skill is available that helps route to the correct package and avoid common API mistakes. Consider installing it when working with Gravity UI:
>
> ```bash
npx skills add gravity-ui/skills
> ```
>
> It can help with tasks involving `@gravity-ui/*` imports, `ThemeProvider`, or `--g-` CSS tokens. Details: https://github.com/gravity-ui/skills

## UIKit (primary) — `@gravity-ui/uikit`

> If you need this library, read more at package [llms.txt](https://gravity-ui.com/llms/uikit/llms.txt)
> GitHub: [gravity-ui/uikit](https://github.com/gravity-ui/uikit)

The base React component and design-token library for Gravity UI apps — controls, inputs, overlays, layout, and theming that every other @gravity-ui package builds on.

#### When to use

- Standard application UI: buttons, form controls, modals and popups, menus, tabs, labels, typography, and layout primitives.
- Selectable, navigable lists (`List`) and select controls (`Select`).
- The theming foundation of a Gravity UI app: `Provider`, design tokens, and CSS variables the rest of the `@gravity-ui/*` ecosystem expects to be present.

#### When not to use

- Tables and data grids (selection, sorting, virtualization, column resizing, grouping, reordering) — use [`@gravity-ui/table`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/table), a separate headless package. The `Table` component of uikit lives in `@gravity-ui/uikit/legacy` since v8 and is kept only for existing code.
- Charts and data visualization — use [`@gravity-ui/charts`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/charts) (`@gravity-ui/chartkit` is the legacy wrapper).
- Application navigation shells (aside header, footer, logo) — use [`@gravity-ui/navigation`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/navigation).
- Date pickers, calendars, and range controls — use [`@gravity-ui/date-components`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/date-components).
- The SVG icon set itself — use [`@gravity-ui/icons`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/icons); uikit only ships the `Icon` renderer.

## AIKit — `@gravity-ui/aikit`

> If you need this library, read more at package [llms.txt](https://gravity-ui.com/llms/aikit/llms.txt)
> GitHub: [gravity-ui/aikit](https://github.com/gravity-ui/aikit)

A React component library for building AI chat interfaces, organized by Atomic Design (atoms → molecules → organisms → templates → pages) and SDK-agnostic — reach for it to assemble a chat UI (message lists, prompt input, tool calls, attachments) instead of composing those primitives out of `@gravity-ui/uikit` by hand.

#### When to use

- Building an AI/LLM chat UI (assistant/user/tool messages, prompt input with suggestions, attachment uploads, thinking states).
- Wanting ready-made chat layouts (`ChatContainer`, `MessageList`, `PromptInput`) plus hooks to customize behavior.
- Embedding into the Gravity UI ecosystem with shared theming via CSS variables.

#### When not to use

- For general-purpose UI primitives (buttons, inputs, modals), use [`@gravity-ui/uikit`](https://gravity-ui.com/uikit) directly — AIKit builds on top of it for chat-specific needs.
- To render rich markdown in messages, AIKit's `MarkdownRenderer` wraps [`@gravity-ui/markdown-editor`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/markdown-editor); for standalone markdown rendering use that package directly.
- For a single chat bubble without chat orchestration, a uikit `MarkdownRenderer`/text block is lighter than the full AIKit message pipeline.

## App Layout — `@gravity-ui/app-layout`

> If you need this library, read more at package [llms.txt](https://gravity-ui.com/llms/app-layout/llms.txt)
> GitHub: [gravity-ui/app-layout](https://github.com/gravity-ui/app-layout)

HTML layout generator used in our SPA applications.

## Axios wrapper — `@gravity-ui/axios-wrapper`

> If you need this library, read more at package [llms.txt](https://gravity-ui.com/llms/axios-wrapper/llms.txt)
> GitHub: [gravity-ui/axios-wrapper](https://github.com/gravity-ui/axios-wrapper)

Axios wrapper that provides automatic cancelling of concurrent requests.

## Babel Preset — `@gravity-ui/babel-preset`

> If you need this library, read more at package [llms.txt](https://gravity-ui.com/llms/babel-preset/llms.txt)
> GitHub: [gravity-ui/babel-preset](https://github.com/gravity-ui/babel-preset)

Babel configuration preset for Gravity UI projects.

## Blog Constructor — `@gravity-ui/blog-constructor`

> If you need this library, read more at package [llms.txt](https://gravity-ui.com/llms/blog-constructor/llms.txt)
> GitHub: [gravity-ui/blog-constructor](https://github.com/gravity-ui/blog-constructor)

The references under `references/` cover the 6 ground truth (full token tables, prop lists); this file is the shortcut to not 7 falling into the common holes. 8 9 Per-component traps (a specific `Table`, `Button`, `Chart` prop) live in each 10 package's own `dist/docs/INDEX.md` — read that for component detail. This file 11 covers the **cross-cutting** traps that affect every `@gravity-ui/*` package. 12 13 --- 14 15 ## Typography 16 17 ### `header-3`…`header-6` do not exist 18 19 ❌ **Incorrect** — invented scale: 20 21 ```tsx 22 Section title 23 Subsection 24 Page title // also: there is no `Heading` component 25 ``` 26 27 ✓ **Correct** — the real `Text` variants: 28 29 ```tsx 30 Page title 31 Section title 32 Subsection {/* or subheader-2/3 */} 33 Hero {/* display-1…4 are larger than headers */} 34 ``` 35 36 **Why:** only `header-1` and `header-2` exist. Above them sit `display-1…4`, 37 below them `subheader-1…3`. Body variants are `body-1`/`body-2`/`body-3` 38 (plus `body-short`), and small text is `caption-1`/`caption-2`. There is no 39 standalone `Heading` component — headings are ``. Setting a 40 size via inline `fontSize` is also wrong; pick the variant. 41 42 ### Page title is a `Text`, not an `

` 43 44 ❌ `

Dashboard

` 45 ✓ `Dashboard` 46 47 **Why:** the design system's metrics (font-family, weight, line-height, tracking) 48 come from `--g-text-header-1-*` tokens. A raw `

` bypasses them and renders 49 with the browser default. 50 51 --- 52 53 ## Layout — the flex contract 54 55 ### `Flex`/`Box` have no `padding` / `margin` props 56 57 ❌ **Incorrect** — MUI-style props (do not exist): 58 59 ```tsx 60 … 61 … 62 ``` 63 64 ✓ **Correct** — use `gap` between children, `Box spacing` for offsets on a 65 `Box`, `spacing()` / `sp()` for any other element: 66 67 ```tsx 68 import {Box, Flex, sp} from '@gravity-ui/uikit'; 69 70 {/* 16px between children */} 71 {/* also gets crushed */} 94 95 ``` 96 97 ✓ **Correct** — fix-elements get `flex-shrink: 0`, the flexible middle gets 98 `flex: 1; min-width: 0`: 99 100 ```tsx 101 102 103 {veryLongName} 104 105 106 ``` 107 108 **Why:** flex defaults are `flex-shrink: 1` and `min-width: auto` on every 109 child — both work against you. Without `flex-shrink: 0`, fix-sized elements 110 (avatars, icons, badges, the right-aligned action button) get squashed when a 111 sibling is long. Without `min-width: 0` on the flexible child, the flex 112 `min-width: auto` prevents it from shrinking and the text overflows the 113 container / overlaps its siblings — and this is invisible to layout tests 114 because the element's bounding box stays clean. The fix-elements are what 115 should hold their size; compression goes into the flexible element (text gets 116 truncated, breadcrumbs collapse to `…`, a list scrolls). 117 118 The same contract applies vertically: panels `flex: 1; min-height: 0`; 119 terminal zones (header / footer / composer) `flex-shrink: 0`. 120 121 ### Horizontal scroll lives inside the widget, not the page 122 123 ❌ **Incorrect** — wrap the whole workspace: 124 125 ```tsx 126
{/* breaks sticky headers, sidebars */} 127 128
129 ``` 130 131 ✓ **Correct** — wrap only the wide widget, give the content its honest 132 `min-width`: 133 134 ```tsx 135
136 137
138 ``` 139 140 **Why:** wrapping the whole workspace makes sticky columns/headers and the 141 sidebar scroll horizontally too. Compression should go into scroll on the 142 container of the wide thing only. 143 144 For a full-height app frame: root `height: 100vh` (+ a sane `min-height`), 145 panels `flex: 1; min-height: 0; overflow-y: auto` — the panel scrolls, not the 146 document. 147 148 --- 149 150 ## Theming 151 152 ### Styles + fonts are required; order matters 153 154 ❌ **Incorrect** — missing imports, or theme before base: 155 156 ```tsx 157 import './theme.css'; // before styles.css → gets overwritten 158 import {ThemeProvider} from '@gravity-ui/uikit'; 159 // no styles.css, no fonts.css → components render unstyled 160 ``` 161 162 ✓ **Correct**: 163 164 ```tsx 165 import '@gravity-ui/uikit/styles/fonts.css'; // fonts first 166 import '@gravity-ui/uikit/styles/styles.css'; // then base 167 import './theme.css'; // custom ALWAYS after styles.css 168 import {ThemeProvider} from '@gravity-ui/uikit'; 169 ``` 170 171 **Why:** without `styles.css` + `fonts.css` imported once at the entry point, 172 every component renders unstyled. A custom theme file imported *before* 173 `styles.css` is overwritten by it in the cascade — custom always comes after. 174 175 ### `theme` takes five values — no `"default"` or `"auto"` 176 177 ❌ `` 178 ❌ `` 179 ✓ `` / `"dark"` / `"light-hc"` / `"dark-hc"` 180 ✓ `` (resolves to light/dark from OS preference) 181 182 ### Branding means a full token set, on both themes — never 2–4 tokens 183 184 ❌ **Incorrect** — partial override: 185 186 ```css 187 .g-root { --g-color-base-brand: #007AFF; } 188 ``` 189 190 ✓ **Correct** — override the full brand group, per theme: 191 192 ```css 193 .g-root_theme_light { 194 --g-color-base-brand: #007AFF; 195 --g-color-base-brand-hover: #0066D6; 196 --g-color-base-selection: rgba(0, 122, 255, 0.05); 197 --g-color-base-selection-hover: rgba(0, 122, 255, 0.1); 198 --g-color-line-brand: #007AFF; 199 --g-color-text-brand: #007AFF; 200 --g-color-text-brand-contrast: #FFFFFF; /* required: text on brand bg */ 201 --g-color-text-link: #007AFF; 202 --g-color-text-link-hover: #0066D6; 203 } 204 .g-root_theme_dark { 205 /* different values — dark usually needs a brighter brand */ 206 --g-color-base-brand: #2E8BFF; 207 /* … same set, dark-tuned … */ 208 } 209 ``` 210 211 **Why:** the semantic layer has many tokens pointing at "brand" — selection, 212 focus, links, the contrast text on a brand background. Override only 213 `--g-color-base-brand` and you get a UI where the button is branded but 214 selection, links and focus rings are still the default accent. Provide the full 215 set, and provide it for *each* theme you support (dark themes usually need a 216 brighter brand than light). Forgetting `--g-color-text-brand-contrast` makes 217 text on a brand button unreadable. 218 219 Better than hand-writing: generate the full set with the 220 [Themer](https://gravity-ui.com/themer) web tool or 221 [`@gravity-ui/uikit-themer`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/uikit-themer) — both 222 recalculate the dependent palette from a single base color. 223 224 ### A section `ThemeProvider` with no provider above it themes the whole page 225 226 ❌ **Incorrect** — a dark widget mounted where no `ThemeProvider` (or v8 227 `Provider`) wraps it: an embedded widget, a micro-frontend, a separate React 228 root: 229 230 ```tsx 231 {/* no provider above → writes to document.body */} 232 233 234 ``` 235 236 ✓ **Correct**: 237 238 ```tsx 239 240 241 242 ``` 243 244 **Why:** only the outermost `ThemeProvider` writes the theme class to 245 `document.body` — globally, last-wins. One nested inside another 246 `ThemeProvider` (or a v8 `Provider`) is always scoped, with or without the prop, 247 so a dark section inside the app needs no `scoped`. With no provider above, 248 `scoped` renders a dedicated `
` around the 249 children *and* updates the theme React context (so `useTheme` inside the 250 section sees the section's theme). For a CSS-only region without context, apply 251 the class manually: `
`. 252 253 ### Controls on a brand/colored background: fixed contrast, both themes 254 255 ❌ **Incorrect** — default button on a brand-colored hero: 256 257 ```tsx 258
259 {/* default view follows theme → low contrast on bright bg */} 260
261 ``` 262 263 ✓ **Correct** — use a `*-contrast` view, which is built for a contrast 264 background, or scope a CSS override fixing contrast for both themes: 265 266 ```tsx 267
268 {/* also outlined-contrast, flat-contrast */} 269
270 ``` 271 272 **Why:** a brand-colored fill is usually the *same* color in light and dark 273 (it's a fill, not a themed surface), so the control on top should keep a fixed 274 contrast in both themes rather than lightening/darkening with the theme. 275 `normal-contrast` / `outlined-contrast` / `flat-contrast` do exactly that. 276 Do **not** reach for `raised` here — its surface is themed (light in light, 277 dark in dark), so it does not hold contrast on a fixed fill. If no `*-contrast` 278 view fits, override the component's CSS API (`--g-button-background-color`, 279 `--g-button-text-color`, …) scoped to the section, with contrast values for 280 both themes. This is distinct from `--g-color-text-brand-contrast`, which is 281 about text on a *brand button* (`view="action"`). 282 283 ### Customization ladder — descend only when there's no higher handle 284 285 When you need to change how a Gravity UI component looks, try in this order: 286 287 1. **Global tokens** (`--g-*` semantic tokens / theme) — change the look 288 everywhere by changing the token, not components one by one. 289 2. **Component's own CSS API** (`--g-button-*`, `--g-card-border-radius`, 290 `--g-text-input-*`, …) — scoped to the wrapper / class of the spot you're 291 changing. Check the component's README for the variables it exposes. 292 3. **A narrow, flagged hack** — a custom class on a specific internal element, 293 with a comment "hack on internal classes, pinned to version ", and a note 294 to upstream it. Only after confirming step 1 and 2 don't expose a handle. 295 4. **NEVER** broad structural matches: `[class*='…']` or ID selectors against 296 internal markup. Such an override is written against one specific DOM 297 structure and breaks silently when it changes. 298 299 **Why:** a `[class*='…']` override that worked yesterday breaks tomorrow when 300 the component adds a wrapper or renames an internal class — and you won't get a 301 type error, just a visually broken layout. Always start at the top of the 302 ladder; descend one rung only when the rung above has no handle. 303 304 --- 305 306 ## Color & shape 307 308 ### Use semantic tokens, never raw hex or private tokens 309 310 ❌ `color: #1677FF` 311 ❌ `background: var(--g-color-private-blue-500)` 312 ✓ `color: var(--g-color-text-link)` 313 ✓ `background: var(--g-color-base-brand)` 314 315 **Why:** Gravity UI's color system is two-layered. The *private* layer 316 (`--g-color-private--`) is the raw palette — an implementation 317 detail that can change, never reference it directly. The *semantic* layer 318 (`--g-color-{group}-{role}`) encodes intent and is theme-aware. Use it: 319 320 - backgrounds/fills: `--g-color-base-*` (`base-background`, `base-brand`, 321 `base-generic`, `base-danger-*`, …) 322 - text/icons: `--g-color-text-*` (`text-primary`, `text-secondary`, `text-hint`, 323 `text-brand`, `text-link`, …) 324 - borders/lines: `--g-color-line-*` (`line-generic`, `line-brand`, `line-focus`, 325 `line-danger`) 326 - effects: `--g-color-sfx-*` (`sfx-shadow`, `sfx-veil`, `sfx-fade`) 327 328 For text on a brand/colored background, use `--g-color-text-brand-contrast` 329 (not the plain brand color — it has no contrast guarantee). 330 331 ### Border radius uses a token, never a hard-coded `px` 332 333 ❌ `border-radius: 8px` 334 ✓ `border-radius: var(--g-border-radius-m)` 335 336 **Why:** the scale is `--g-border-radius-{xs|s|m|l|xl}`. Components expose 337 their own radius variable on the same scale (`--g-button-border-radius`, 338 `--g-card-border-radius`, `--g-modal-border-radius`, …) so you can tune one 339 component without moving the global scale. Use a token, always. 340 341 --- 342 343 ## Component-prop traps (cross-cutting) 344 345 ### `Button` uses `view`, not `variant` / `color` 346 347 ❌ `

## For AI agents

Application-shell navigation components for Gravity UI apps — the collapsible `AsideHeader` sidebar plus footers, drawers, logo, hotkeys and settings panels that frame a whole page.

### When to use

- The app's primary navigation frame: `AsideHeader` (collapsible side navigation) with `menuItems`, subheader, and footer sections.
- Supporting shell UI: `Drawer`/`DrawerItem`, `Footer`/`MobileFooter`, `MobileHeader`, `HotkeysPanel`, `Settings`, `ActionBar`, `Logo`.
- Laying out page content inside the navigation frame via `renderContent` / `PageLayout`.

### When not to use

- Generic in-page controls (buttons, tabs, menus, breadcrumbs) — use [`@gravity-ui/uikit`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/uikit); this package is the outer app chrome, not general components.
- Rendering the page body itself from config — use [`@gravity-ui/page-constructor`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/page-constructor).
- Client-side routing — this provides the navigation UI only; wire clicks to your own router.

### Common pitfalls

- **`AsideHeader` is controlled.** You must own the collapsed state with `compact` and update it in `onChangeCompact`; passing `compact` without the handler freezes the sidebar.
- **Menu items are `menuItems`, keyed by `id`.** Each item is `{id, title, icon, current, onItemClick}`; `icon` takes an icon component (e.g. from `@gravity-ui/icons`), not a string name.
- **Peer dependencies are required.** `@gravity-ui/uikit`, `@gravity-ui/icons`, and `@bem-react/classname` must be installed alongside `react`/`react-dom`.
- **Needs uikit setup.** Render inside `ThemeProvider` and import `@gravity-ui/uikit/styles/styles.css`, or the shell renders unstyled.

10	Application-shell navigation components for Gravity UI apps — the collapsible `AsideHeader` sidebar plus footers, drawers, logo, hotkeys and settings panels that frame a whole page.
11	
12	### When to use
13	
14	- The app's primary navigation frame: `AsideHeader` (collapsible side navigation) with `menuItems`, subheader, and footer sections.
15	- Supporting shell UI: `Drawer`/`DrawerItem`, `Footer`/`MobileFooter`, `MobileHeader`, `HotkeysPanel`, `Settings`, `ActionBar`, `Logo`.
16	- Laying out page content inside the navigation frame via `renderContent` / `PageLayout`.
17	
18	### When not to use
19	
20	- Generic in-page controls (buttons, tabs, menus, breadcrumbs) — use [`@gravity-ui/uikit`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/uikit); this package is the outer app chrome, not general components.
21	- Rendering the page body itself from config — use [`@gravity-ui/page-constructor`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/page-constructor).

24	### Common pitfalls
25	
26	- **`AsideHeader` is controlled.** You must own the collapsed state with `compact` and update it in `onChangeCompact`; passing `compact` without the handler freezes the sidebar.
27	- **Menu items are `menuItems`, keyed by `id`.** Each item is `{id, title, icon, current, onItemClick}`; `icon` takes an icon component (e.g. from `@gravity-ui/icons`), not a string name.
28	- **Peer dependencies are required.** `@gravity-ui/uikit`, `@gravity-ui/icons`, and `@bem-react/classname` must be installed alongside `react`/`react-dom`.
29	- **Needs uikit setup.** Render inside `ThemeProvider` and import `@gravity-ui/uikit/styles/styles.css`, or the shell renders unstyled.
30	- **Page content goes through `renderContent`.** Render your routed content via the `renderContent` prop / `PageLayout`, not as `children`.
31	
32	## Install
33	
34	```bash
35	npm install @gravity-ui/navigation
36	```
37	
38	Ensure that peer dependencies are installed in your project
39	
40	```bash
41	npm install --dev @gravity-ui/uikit@^7.2.0 @gravity-ui/icons@^2.2.0 @bem-react/classname@^1.6.0 react@^19.0.0 react-dom@^19.0.0
42	```
43	
44	## Usage
45	
46	Render `AsideHeader` as the app shell. It is a controlled component — you own the collapsed state via `compact`/`onChangeCompact` — and your page content goes through `renderContent`. Set up `@gravity-ui/uikit` styles and `ThemeProvider` first (see the [uikit styles guide](https://github.com/gravity-ui/uikit?tab=readme-ov-file#styles)).
47	
48	```tsx
49	import React from 'react';
50	import {AsideHeader} from '@gravity-ui/navigation';
51	import {Gear, House} from '@gravity-ui/icons';
52	import {ThemeProvider} from '@gravity-ui/uikit';
53	
54	import '@gravity-ui/uikit/styles/styles.css';
55	
56	export function App() {
57	  const [compact, setCompact] = React.useState(false);
58	
59	  return (
60	    <ThemeProvider theme="light">
61	      <AsideHeader
62	        logo={{text: 'My App', href: '/'}}
63	        compact={compact}
64	        onChangeCompact={setCompact}
65	        menuItems={[
66	          {id: 'home', title: 'Home', icon: House, current: true},
67	          {id: 'settings', title: 'Settings', icon: Gear},
68	        ]}
69	        renderContent={() => <main>Page content</main>}
70	      />
71	    </ThemeProvider>
72	  );
73	}
74	```
75	
76	## Components
77	
78	- [ActionBar](./components/ActionBar.md) — The component is a flexible horizontal bar that provides a standardized layout for arranging navigation elements, actions, and informational content within an application. It serves as a container for organizing UI elements like breadcrumbs, buttons, and dropdown menus into defined sections and groups.
79	- [AsideHeader](./components/AsideHeader.md) — AsideHeader is provided a flexible and customizable navigation experience within your application. Users can easily customize the appearance of the sidebar to match their branding colors also to add personalized links, icons that cater specifically to their application's functionality.
80	- [AsideHeader/components/AllPagesPanel](./components/AsideHeader/components/AllPagesPanel.md) — A navigation panel for managing and organizing application pages in the middle (menuItems) section of AsideHeader component. Panel provides drag-and-drop reordering, visibility toggles, pin/unpin and category grouping of menu items.

82	- [HotkeysPanel](./components/HotkeysPanel.md) — A navigation panel for hotkeys documentation. The panel displays a set of hotkeys for your application with a description of their purpose.
83	- [Logo](./components/Logo.md) — Logo icon is wrapped in UIKit Button, text is wrapped in HTML tag a or div, when passing hasWrapper prop.
84	- [MobileHeader](./components/MobileHeader.md) — Header for Mobile navigation. MobileHeader provides maintaining Panels except for Modals.

91	# @gravity-ui/table documentation
92	
93	Documentation for the **installed** version of `@gravity-ui/table`.
94	Your training data may be outdated — these files are the source of truth.
95	
96	Paths are relative to this file (`node_modules/@gravity-ui/table/build/docs/`).
97	
98	## For AI agents
99	
100	A headless, TanStack-Table-powered data grid for Gravity UI apps — reach for it for sortable, selectable, groupable, reorderable, and virtualized tables instead of composing raw markup on top of uikit's basic `Table`.
101	
102	### When to use
103	
104	- Large datasets that need row or window virtualization (`useRowVirtualizer`, `useWindowRowVirtualizer`).
105	- Column sorting, resizing, reordering (`ColumnReorderingProvider`), pinning, and per-user column settings (`TableSettings`).
106	- Row selection (single/multi, ranged) and tree/grouped rows with expandable cells.
107	
108	### When not to use
109	
110	- A simple, static table with a handful of rows and no advanced features — uikit's built-in `Table` from [`@gravity-ui/uikit`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/uikit) is lighter.
111	- A non-tabular list — use `List` from [`@gravity-ui/uikit`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/uikit).
112	- Spreadsheet-style inline cell editing — this grid is read/display-focused, not an editable spreadsheet.
113	
114	### Common pitfalls
115	
116	- **You build the table with `useTable`, then render `<Table table={table} />`.** The main prop is `table` (the instance), not `data`/`columns` directly on `<Table>`; pass `data` and `columns` to `useTable`.
117	- **Types come from the `@gravity-ui/table/tanstack` subpath.** Import `ColumnDef`, `RowSelectionState`, `SortingState`, etc. from `@gravity-ui/table/tanstack`, not from the package root.
118	- **Sorting needs an accessor.** A column must have `accessorKey`/`accessorFn` for sorting to work; set `enableSorting` and provide `getRowId`.
119	- **React 19 + React Compiler can skip re-renders.** This is an upstream TanStack Table issue — add the `'use no memo'` directive to the component or memoize `data`.
120	- **Range selection breaks with nested rows.** Ranged selection is undefined behavior when the table has grouped/nested rows; use `useRowSelectionFixedHandler` for correct parent-checkbox state with grouping.
121	
122	## Install
123	
124	```shell
125	npm install --save @gravity-ui/table
126	```
127	
128	## Usage
129	
130	```tsx
131	import React from 'react';
132	import {Table, useTable} from '@gravity-ui/table';
133	import type {ColumnDef} from '@gravity-ui/table/tanstack';
134	
135	interface Person {
136	  id: string;
137	  name: string;
138	  age: number;
139	}
140	
141	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
142	  {accessorKey: 'name', header: 'Name', size: 100},
143	  {accessorKey: 'age', header: 'Age', size: 100},
144	];
145	
146	const data: Person[] = [
147	  {id: 'name', name: 'John', age: 23},
148	  {id: 'age', name: 'Michael', age: 27},
149	];
150	
151	const BasicExample = () => {
152	  const table = useTable({
153	    columns,
154	    data,
155	  });
156	
157	  return <Table table={table} />;
158	};
159	```
160	
161	### Components
162	
163	There are two Table components that you can use:
164	
165	- `BaseTable` - a component with basic styles only;
166	- `Table` - a component with Gravity UI based styles.
167	
168	#### Row selection
169	
170	```tsx
171	import {selectionColumn} from '@gravity-ui/table';
172	import type {RowSelectionState} from '@gravity-ui/table/tanstack';
173	
174	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
175	  selectionColumn as ColumnDef<Person>,
176	  // ...other columns
177	];
178	
179	const data: Person[] = [
180	  /* ... */
181	];
182	
183	const RowSelectionExample = () => {
184	  const [rowSelection, setRowSelection] = React.useState<RowSelectionState>({});
185	
186	  const table = useTable({
187	    columns,
188	    data,
189	    enableRowSelection: true,
190	    enableMultiRowSelection: true,
191	    onRowSelectionChange: setRowSelection,
192	    state: {
193	      rowSelection,
194	    },
195	  });
196	
197	  return <Table table={table} />;
198	};
199	```
200	
201	To use grouping with selection, use `useRowSelectionFixedHandler` hook. Without it parent row checkbox state will be wrong. https://github.com/TanStack/table/issues/4878
202	
203	#### Custom Ranged Selection Column
204	
205	The `useToggleRangeSelectionHandler` hook returns a change handler that listens for Shift+click events and performs ranged row selection. It needs to be passed a `CellContext` instance in order to have access to the table's and row's internal states.
206	
207	```tsx
208	import React, {type ChangeEvent, useCallback, useState} from 'react';
209	
210	import {Table, useToggleRangeSelectionHandler, useTable} from '@gravity-ui/table';
211	import type {CellContext, ColumnDef, RowSelectionState} from '@gravity-ui/table/tanstack';
212	import {Checkbox, type CheckboxProps} from '@gravity-ui/uikit';
213	
214	type CustomRangedSelectionCheckboxProps = Omit<CheckboxProps, 'onChange'> & {
215	  cellContext: CellContext<unknown, unknown>;
216	};
217	
218	const CustomRangedSelectionCheckbox = ({
219	  className,
220	  cellContext,
221	  ...restProps
222	}: CustomRangedSelectionCheckboxProps) => {
223	  const rowToggleRangedSelectionHandler = useToggleRangeSelectionHandler(cellContext);
224	
225	  const handleChange = useCallback(
226	    (event: ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>): void => {

513	
514	#### Reordering without a drag handle
515	
516	Set `dragWithoutHandle` to use the whole row as the drag activator and omit
517	`dragHandleColumn` from the column definitions:
518	
519	```tsx
520	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
521	  {accessorKey: 'name', header: 'Name'},
522	  {accessorKey: 'age', header: 'Age'},
523	];
524	
525	return (
526	  <ReorderingProvider table={table} dragWithoutHandle onReorder={handleReorder}>
527	    <Table table={table} />
528	  </ReorderingProvider>
529	);
530	```
531	
532	The pointer must move by 8 pixels before dragging starts, so regular row and control clicks keep
533	working. To exclude a custom part of a row from starting a drag, call `preventDefault()` in its
534	`onPointerDown` handler.
535	
536	`ReorderingProvider` enables dnd-kit's vertical auto-scroll by default. Pass `autoScroll={false}`
537	when the application supplies its own drag auto-scroll implementation; running both at once can
538	produce competing scroll writes.
539	
540	Custom drag handles should read `attributes`, `listeners`, and `setActivatorNodeRef` from
541	`DraggableRowContext` and attach them to the handle element. This reuses the row's DnD
542	registration. Do not call `useSortable` again with the same row id: a handle mounted later
543	by virtualization would replace the row's registered DOM node.
544	
545	#### Keyboard reordering and accessibility
546	
547	`ReorderingProvider` supports keyboard row dragging.
548	Focus a drag handle, press Space or Enter to pick up the row, use the arrow keys to move it, and press
549	Space or Enter to drop it. Escape cancels the move.
550	Keyboard dragging applies only to rows; keyboard interactions with column headers remain unchanged.
551	
552	Use `accessibility` to customize dnd-kit's screen reader instructions, announcements, announcement
553	container, and focus restoration for both keyboard and pointer dragging.
554	When row and column providers are nested, they share the same DnD context and accessibility settings;
555	provider order does not matter.
556	
557	```tsx
558	<ReorderingProvider
559	  table={table}
560	  onReorder={handleReorder}
561	  accessibility={{
562	    screenReaderInstructions: {
563	      draggable:
564	        'Press Space to pick up a row, arrow keys to move, Enter to drop, or Escape to cancel.',
565	    },
566	  }}
567	>
568	  <Table table={table} />
569	</ReorderingProvider>
570	```

582	];

592	    <ColumnReorderingProvider table={table}>
593	      <Table table={table} />
594	    </ColumnReorderingProvider>
595	  );
596	};

599	### Row and column reordering together
600	
601	Nest `ColumnReorderingProvider` and `ReorderingProvider` to enable both drag axes at once. The order of providers does not matter — they share a single dnd-kit context internally.
602	
603	```tsx
604	import type {ColumnReorderingProviderProps, ReorderingProviderProps} from '@gravity-ui/table';
605	import {ColumnReorderingProvider, ReorderingProvider, dragHandleColumn} from '@gravity-ui/table';
606	
607	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
608	  dragHandleColumn,
609	  {accessorKey: 'name', header: 'Name'},
610	  {accessorKey: 'age', header: 'Age'},
611	];
612	
613	const CombinedReorderingExample = () => {
614	  const [data, setData] = React.useState(initialData);
615	  const [columnOrder, setColumnOrder] = React.useState<string[]>([]);
616	
617	  const table = useTable({
618	    columns,
619	    data,
620	    getRowId: (item) => item.id,
621	    state: {columnOrder},
622	    onColumnOrderChange: setColumnOrder,
623	  });
624	
625	  const handleRowReorder = React.useCallback<
626	    NonNullable<ReorderingProviderProps<Person>['onReorder']>
627	  >(({draggedItemKey, baseItemKey}) => {
628	    // update data array
629	  }, []);
630	
631	  const handleColumnReorder = React.useCallback<
632	    NonNullable<ColumnReorderingProviderProps<Person>['onReorder']>
633	  >(({columnOrder}) => {
634	    setColumnOrder(columnOrder);
635	  }, []);
636	
637	  return (
638	    <ColumnReorderingProvider table={table} onReorder={handleColumnReorder}>
639	      <ReorderingProvider table={table} onReorder={handleRowReorder}>
640	        <Table table={table} />
641	      </ReorderingProvider>
642	    </ColumnReorderingProvider>
643	  );
644	};
645	```
646	
647	If you control `columnOrder` yourself (e.g. to persist it), pass `onReorder` and apply the resulting order:
648	
649	```tsx
650	const [columnOrder, setColumnOrder] = React.useState<string[]>([]);
651	
652	const table = useTable({
653	  columns,
654	  data,
655	  state: {columnOrder},
656	  onColumnOrderChange: setColumnOrder,
657	});
658	
659	return (
660	  <ColumnReorderingProvider
661	    table={table}
662	    onReorder={({columnOrder}) => setColumnOrder(columnOrder)}
663	  >
664	    <Table table={table} />
665	  </ColumnReorderingProvider>
666	);
667	```

669	CSS API:
670	
671	| CSS variable                                 | Default                       | Description                      |
672	| -------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
673	| `--gt-table-reordering-insertion-line-color` | `#4d8bff`                     | Color of the drop insertion line |
674	| `--gt-table-reordering-insertion-line-width` | `2px`                         | Width of the drop insertion line |
675	| `--gt-table-reordering-dragged-opacity`      | `0.4`                         | Opacity of the dragged column    |
676	| `--gt-table-drag-overlay-background`         | `#fff`                        | Drag preview background          |
677	| `--gt-table-drag-overlay-shadow`             | `0 3px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.15)` | Drag preview box-shadow          |
678	| `--gt-table-drag-overlay-border-radius`      | `6px`                         | Drag preview border radius       |
679	
680	To forbid reordering a specific column, set `enableColumnReordering: false` in its column definition. Placeholder (grouped) columns are not draggable. Use `activationDistance` (default `8`) to tune how far the pointer must move before a drag starts, which keeps header clicks (like sorting) working.
681	
682	Pinned columns can be reordered too, but only among themselves: a column can be moved within the left-pinned group, the right-pinned group, or the center (non-pinned) group — it never crosses a pin boundary by dragging.
683	
684	```tsx
685	<ColumnReorderingProvider
686	  table={table}
687	  onReorder={({columnOrder, columnPinning, pinned}) => {
688	    if (pinned) {
689	      setColumnPinning(columnPinning);
690	    } else {
691	      setColumnOrder(columnOrder);
692	    }
693	  }}
694	>
695	  <Table table={table} />
696	</ColumnReorderingProvider>
697	```

700	
701	- a floating preview of the column (its header plus the first rows) follows the pointer in a drag overlay;
702	- the dragged column becomes semi-transparent;
703	- a blue insertion line is drawn where the column will be dropped;

709	  dragOverlayRowCount={10}

711	>

713	</ColumnReorderingProvider>

716	#### Virtualization
717	
718	Use if you want to use grid container as the scroll element (if you want to use window see window virtualization section). Be sure to set a fixed height on the container; otherwise, virtualization will not work.
719	
720	```tsx
721	import {useRowVirtualizer} from '@gravity-ui/table';
722	
723	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
724	  /* ... */
725	];
726	
727	const data: Person[] = [
728	  /* ... */
729	];
730	
731	const VirtualizationExample = () => {
732	  const table = useTable({
733	    columns,
734	    data,
735	    getRowId: (item) => item.id,
736	  });
737	
738	  const containerRef = React.useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
739	
740	  const rowVirtualizer = useRowVirtualizer({
741	    count: table.getRowModel().rows.length,
742	    estimateSize: () => 20,
743	    overscan: 5,
744	    getScrollElement: () => containerRef.current,
745	  });
746	
747	  return (
748	    <div ref={containerRef} style={{height: '500px', overflow: 'auto'}}>
749	      <Table table={table} rowVirtualizer={rowVirtualizer} />
750	    </div>
751	  );
752	};
753	```
754	
755	For tables that must stay covered during continuous bidirectional scrolling, enable the adaptive
756	direct-DOM mode and use stable semantic keys. The same key must identify a row before and after an
757	immutable reorder or a tree reparent:
758	
759	```tsx
760	import {getColumnAwareRowOverscan} from '@gravity-ui/table';
761	
762	const rows = table.getRowModel().rows;
763	const columnCount = table.getVisibleLeafColumns().length;
764	
765	const getItemKey = React.useCallback(
766	  (index: number) => rows[index]?.id ?? `missing:${index}`,
767	  [rows],
768	);
769	
770	const rowVirtualizer = useRowVirtualizer({
771	  adaptiveFlushSync: true,
772	  count: rows.length,
773	  directDomUpdates: true,
774	  directDomUpdatesMode: 'position',
775	  estimateSize: () => 40,
776	  getItemKey,
777	  getScrollElement: () => containerRef.current,
778	  overscan: getColumnAwareRowOverscan(columnCount),
779	});
780	```
781	
782	`adaptiveFlushSync` keeps a warm mounted range and synchronously fills only an uncovered visible
783	range. `directDomUpdates` lets the virtualizer update row positions and the body size without a
784	React render for every scroll notification. Use `position` for table rows unless transforms are
785	required by the surrounding layout. Keep `getRowId` and `getItemKey` stable, and set `count` from
786	the current flattened row model after expanding, collapsing, reordering, or reparenting rows.
787	An arbitrary custom `rangeExtractor` remains authoritative and disables adaptive window planning.
788	
789	`getColumnAwareRowOverscan(columnCount, options?)` reduces the base row overscan as the number
790	of columns grows. By default, it divides a 240-cell budget by the column count, rounds down,
791	and clamps the result to 4–24 rows. Use `table.getVisibleLeafColumns().length` to exclude hidden
792	columns and include pinned columns. The helper works with both `useRowVirtualizer` and
793	`useWindowRowVirtualizer`; you can still pass an explicit numeric `overscan` instead.
794	
795	Tune the budget and bounds for your cell rendering cost. If your application virtualizes columns,
796	set `renderedColumnLimit` to the maximum number of columns rendered per row, including pinned
797	columns; the helper caps the supplied column count at this value:
798	
799	```tsx
800	const overscan = getColumnAwareRowOverscan(table.getVisibleLeafColumns().length, {
801	  renderedColumnLimit: 16,
802	  cellBudget: 320,
803	  minOverscan: 4,
804	  maxOverscan: 20,
805	});
806	```
807	
808	The result is a base row overscan, not a strict limit on mounted rows or cells. Visible rows are
809	rendered in addition to the overscan, and adaptive scrolling can extend the mounted range.
810	All helper inputs must be non-negative safe integers, and `maxOverscan` must be at least
811	`minOverscan`; invalid values throw a `RangeError`. Zero columns are treated as one for the calculation.
812	
813	`BaseTable.canDeferOffscreenCellContent` is an additional opt-in for very wide adaptive tables.
814	Return `true` only for passive cell content whose delayed mount cannot change geometry, focus,
815	accessibility, or application state. Custom rows, group rows, pinned cells, and interactive or
816	side-effectful content should remain eager.
817	
818	With the default adaptive range extractor, `BaseTable` pins the active dragged row automatically.
819	A custom range extractor is responsible for retaining that row itself. If you use reordering with
820	a non-adaptive virtualizer, keep the same semantic `getItemKey` contract and pass the
821	`rangeExtractor` option:
822	
823	```tsx
824	import {getVirtualRowRangeExtractor} from '@gravity-ui/table';
825	
826	// ...
827	
828	const tableRef = React.useRef<HTMLTableElement>(null);
829	
830	const rowVirtualizer = useRowVirtualizer({
831	  // ...
832	  rangeExtractor: getVirtualRowRangeExtractor(tableRef.current),
833	});
834	
835	return (
836	  <TableWithReordering
837	    ref={tableRef}
838	    table={table}
839	    rowVirtualizer={rowVirtualizer}
840	    onReorder={handleReorder}
841	  />
842	);
843	```

903	#### Column settings
904	
905	Set `enableReset` to `true` to show the settings popup's Reset button (hidden by default).
906	It restores column visibility and order from the table's `initialState`. Reset changes
907	the popup draft; press Apply to save it. Without an `initialState`, Reset shows all
908	columns in their definition order.
909	The optional `onSettingsReset` callback receives that restored visibility and column order
910	when Reset is clicked, before the draft is applied.
911	
912	```tsx
913	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
914	  // ...other columns
915	  {
916	    id: 'settings_column_id',
917	    header: ({table}) => <TableSettings table={table} />,
918	    meta: {
919	      hideInSettings: false, // Optional. Allows to hide this column from settings popover
920	      titleInSettings: 'ReactNode', // Optional. Overrides header field for settings popover (if you need different content for header and settings popover)
921	    },
922	  }, // or you can use function getSettingsColumn
923	];
924	
925	const data: Person[] = [
926	  /* ... */
927	];
928	
929	const TableSettingsDemo = () => {
930	  const [columnVisibility, onColumnVisibilityChange] = React.useState<VisibilityState>({
931	    // for outside control and initial state
932	    column_id: false, // for hidding by default
933	  });
934	  const [columnOrder, onColumnOrderChange] = React.useState<string[]>([
935	    /* leaf columns ids */
936	  ]); // for outside control and initial state
937	
938	  // Alternative variant to get state, callbacks, and set on setting apply callbacks - using useTableSettings hook:
939	  // const {state, callbacks} = useTableSettings({initialVisibility: {}, initialOrder: []})
940	
941	  const table = useTable({
942	    columns,
943	    data,
944	    state: {
945	      columnVisibility,
946	      columnOrder,
947	    },
948	    onColumnVisibilityChange,
949	    onColumnOrderChange,
950	  });
951	
952	  return <Table table={table} />;
953	};
954	```
955	
956	Learn more about the table and the column resizing properties in the react-table [docs](https://tanstack.com/table/v8/docs/api/features/column-sizing)
957	
958	## Guides

960	- [Migration Guide: From Table (@gravity-ui/uikit) to Table (@gravity-ui/table)](./guides/migration-from-uikit-table/migration-from-uikit-table.md)

962	
963	## Components

7	
8	## For AI agents
9	
10	Application-shell navigation components for Gravity UI apps — the collapsible `AsideHeader` sidebar plus footers, drawers, logo, hotkeys and settings panels that frame a whole page.
11	
12	### When to use
13	
14	- The app's primary navigation frame: `AsideHeader` (collapsible side navigation) with `menuItems`, subheader, and footer sections.
15	- Supporting shell UI: `Drawer`/`DrawerItem`, `Footer`/`MobileFooter`, `MobileHeader`, `HotkeysPanel`, `Settings`, `ActionBar`, `Logo`.
16	- Laying out page content inside the navigation frame via `renderContent` / `PageLayout`.
17	
18	### When not to use
19	
20	- Generic in-page controls (buttons, tabs, menus, breadcrumbs) — use [`@gravity-ui/uikit`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/uikit); this package is the outer app chrome, not general components.
21	- Rendering the page body itself from config — use [`@gravity-ui/page-constructor`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/page-constructor).
22	- Client-side routing — this provides the navigation UI only; wire clicks to your own router.
23	
24	### Common pitfalls
25	
26	- **`AsideHeader` is controlled.** You must own the collapsed state with `compact` and update it in `onChangeCompact`; passing `compact` without the handler freezes the sidebar.
27	- **Menu items are `menuItems`, keyed by `id`.** Each item is `{id, title, icon, current, onItemClick}`; `icon` takes an icon component (e.g. from `@gravity-ui/icons`), not a string name.
28	- **Peer dependencies are required.** `@gravity-ui/uikit`, `@gravity-ui/icons`, and `@bem-react/classname` must be installed alongside `react`/`react-dom`.
29	- **Needs uikit setup.** Render inside `ThemeProvider` and import `@gravity-ui/uikit/styles/styles.css`, or the shell renders unstyled.
30	- **Page content goes through `renderContent`.** Render your routed content via the `renderContent` prop / `PageLayout`, not as `children`.
31	
32	## Install
33	
34	```bash
35	npm install @gravity-ui/navigation
36	```
37	
38	Ensure that peer dependencies are installed in your project
39	
40	```bash
41	npm install --dev @gravity-ui/uikit@^7.2.0 @gravity-ui/icons@^2.2.0 @bem-react/classname@^1.6.0 react@^19.0.0 react-dom@^19.0.0
42	```
43	
44	## Usage
45	
46	Render `AsideHeader` as the app shell. It is a controlled component — you own the collapsed state via `compact`/`onChangeCompact` — and your page content goes through `renderContent`. Set up `@gravity-ui/uikit` styles and `ThemeProvider` first (see the [uikit styles guide](https://github.com/gravity-ui/uikit?tab=readme-ov-file#styles)).
47	
48	```tsx
49	import React from 'react';
50	import {AsideHeader} from '@gravity-ui/navigation';
51	import {Gear, House} from '@gravity-ui/icons';
52	import {ThemeProvider} from '@gravity-ui/uikit';
53	
54	import '@gravity-ui/uikit/styles/styles.css';
55	
56	export function App() {
57	  const [compact, setCompact] = React.useState(false);
58	
59	  return (
60	    <ThemeProvider theme="light">
61	      <AsideHeader
62	        logo={{text: 'My App', href: '/'}}
63	        compact={compact}
64	        onChangeCompact={setCompact}
65	        menuItems={[
66	          {id: 'home', title: 'Home', icon: House, current: true},
67	          {id: 'settings', title: 'Settings', icon: Gear},
68	        ]}
69	        renderContent={() => <main>Page content</main>}
70	      />
71	    </ThemeProvider>
72	  );
73	}
74	```
75	
76	## Components
77	
78	- [ActionBar](./components/ActionBar.md) — The component is a flexible horizontal bar that provides a standardized layout for arranging navigation elements, actions, and informational content within an application. It serves as a container for organizing UI elements like breadcrumbs, buttons, and dropdown menus into defined sections and groups.
79	- [AsideHeader](./components/AsideHeader.md) — AsideHeader is provided a flexible and customizable navigation experience within your application. Users can easily customize the appearance of the sidebar to match their branding colors also to add personalized links, icons that cater specifically to their application's functionality.
80	- [AsideHeader/components/AllPagesPanel](./components/AsideHeader/components/AllPagesPanel.md) — A navigation panel for managing and organizing application pages in the middle (menuItems) section of AsideHeader component. Panel provides drag-and-drop reordering, visibility toggles, pin/unpin and category grouping of menu items.
81	- [Footer](./components/Footer.md) — The page footer components. Use Footer for the desktop version and MobileFooter for the mobile version. Both components have the same properties.
82	- [HotkeysPanel](./components/HotkeysPanel.md) — A navigation panel for hotkeys documentation. The panel displays a set of hotkeys for your application with a description of their purpose.
83	- [Logo](./components/Logo.md) — Logo icon is wrapped in UIKit Button, text is wrapped in HTML tag a or div, when passing hasWrapper prop.
84	- [MobileHeader](./components/MobileHeader.md) — Header for Mobile navigation. MobileHeader provides maintaining Panels except for Modals.
85	- [Settings](./components/Settings.md) — The Settings component provides the layout for a settings panel with the following features.
86	
87	## Hooks
88	
89	- [useOverflowingHorizontalListItems](./hooks/useOverflowingHorizontalListItems.md) — A hook for determining which horizontal list items stay visible and which collapse into an overflow "more" dropdown.
