91	# @gravity-ui/table documentation
92	
93	Documentation for the **installed** version of `@gravity-ui/table`.
94	Your training data may be outdated — these files are the source of truth.
95	
96	Paths are relative to this file (`node_modules/@gravity-ui/table/build/docs/`).
97	
98	## For AI agents
99	
100	A headless, TanStack-Table-powered data grid for Gravity UI apps — reach for it for sortable, selectable, groupable, reorderable, and virtualized tables instead of composing raw markup on top of uikit's basic `Table`.
101	
102	### When to use
103	
104	- Large datasets that need row or window virtualization (`useRowVirtualizer`, `useWindowRowVirtualizer`).
105	- Column sorting, resizing, reordering (`ColumnReorderingProvider`), pinning, and per-user column settings (`TableSettings`).
106	- Row selection (single/multi, ranged) and tree/grouped rows with expandable cells.
107	
108	### When not to use
109	
110	- A simple, static table with a handful of rows and no advanced features — uikit's built-in `Table` from [`@gravity-ui/uikit`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/uikit) is lighter.
111	- A non-tabular list — use `List` from [`@gravity-ui/uikit`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/uikit).
112	- Spreadsheet-style inline cell editing — this grid is read/display-focused, not an editable spreadsheet.
113	
114	### Common pitfalls
115	
116	- **You build the table with `useTable`, then render `<Table table={table} />`.** The main prop is `table` (the instance), not `data`/`columns` directly on `<Table>`; pass `data` and `columns` to `useTable`.
117	- **Types come from the `@gravity-ui/table/tanstack` subpath.** Import `ColumnDef`, `RowSelectionState`, `SortingState`, etc. from `@gravity-ui/table/tanstack`, not from the package root.
118	- **Sorting needs an accessor.** A column must have `accessorKey`/`accessorFn` for sorting to work; set `enableSorting` and provide `getRowId`.
119	- **React 19 + React Compiler can skip re-renders.** This is an upstream TanStack Table issue — add the `'use no memo'` directive to the component or memoize `data`.
120	- **Range selection breaks with nested rows.** Ranged selection is undefined behavior when the table has grouped/nested rows; use `useRowSelectionFixedHandler` for correct parent-checkbox state with grouping.
121	
122	## Install
123	
124	```shell
125	npm install --save @gravity-ui/table
126	```
127	
128	## Usage
129	
130	```tsx
131	import React from 'react';
132	import {Table, useTable} from '@gravity-ui/table';
133	import type {ColumnDef} from '@gravity-ui/table/tanstack';
134	
135	interface Person {
136	  id: string;
137	  name: string;
138	  age: number;
139	}
140	
141	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
142	  {accessorKey: 'name', header: 'Name', size: 100},
143	  {accessorKey: 'age', header: 'Age', size: 100},
144	];
145	
146	const data: Person[] = [
147	  {id: 'name', name: 'John', age: 23},
148	  {id: 'age', name: 'Michael', age: 27},
149	];
150	
151	const BasicExample = () => {
152	  const table = useTable({
153	    columns,
154	    data,
155	  });
156	
157	  return <Table table={table} />;
158	};
159	```
160	
161	### Components
162	
163	There are two Table components that you can use:
164	
165	- `BaseTable` - a component with basic styles only;
166	- `Table` - a component with Gravity UI based styles.
167	
168	#### Row selection
169	
170	```tsx
171	import {selectionColumn} from '@gravity-ui/table';
172	import type {RowSelectionState} from '@gravity-ui/table/tanstack';
173	
174	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
175	  selectionColumn as ColumnDef<Person>,
176	  // ...other columns
177	];
178	
179	const data: Person[] = [
180	  /* ... */
181	];
182	
183	const RowSelectionExample = () => {
184	  const [rowSelection, setRowSelection] = React.useState<RowSelectionState>({});
185	
186	  const table = useTable({
187	    columns,
188	    data,
189	    enableRowSelection: true,
190	    enableMultiRowSelection: true,
191	    onRowSelectionChange: setRowSelection,
192	    state: {
193	      rowSelection,
194	    },
195	  });
196	
197	  return <Table table={table} />;
198	};
199	```
200	
201	To use grouping with selection, use `useRowSelectionFixedHandler` hook. Without it parent row checkbox state will be wrong. https://github.com/TanStack/table/issues/4878
202	
203	#### Custom Ranged Selection Column
204	
205	The `useToggleRangeSelectionHandler` hook returns a change handler that listens for Shift+click events and performs ranged row selection. It needs to be passed a `CellContext` instance in order to have access to the table's and row's internal states.
206	
207	```tsx
208	import React, {type ChangeEvent, useCallback, useState} from 'react';
209	
210	import {Table, useToggleRangeSelectionHandler, useTable} from '@gravity-ui/table';
211	import type {CellContext, ColumnDef, RowSelectionState} from '@gravity-ui/table/tanstack';
212	import {Checkbox, type CheckboxProps} from '@gravity-ui/uikit';
213	
214	type CustomRangedSelectionCheckboxProps = Omit<CheckboxProps, 'onChange'> & {
215	  cellContext: CellContext<unknown, unknown>;
216	};
217	
218	const CustomRangedSelectionCheckbox = ({
219	  className,
220	  cellContext,
221	  ...restProps
222	}: CustomRangedSelectionCheckboxProps) => {
223	  const rowToggleRangedSelectionHandler = useToggleRangeSelectionHandler(cellContext);
224	
225	  const handleChange = useCallback(
226	    (event: ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>): void => {
227	      rowToggleRangedSelectionHandler(event);
228	    },
229	    [rowToggleRangedSelectionHandler],
230	  );
231	
232	  return <Checkbox {...restProps} onChange={handleChange} />;
233	};
234	
235	const customSelectionColumn: ColumnDef<unknown> = {
236	  id: '_select',
237	  header: ({table}) => (
238	    <Checkbox
239	      size="l"
240	      checked={table.getIsAllRowsSelected()}
241	      indeterminate={table.getIsSomeRowsSelected()}
242	      onChange={table.getToggleAllRowsSelectedHandler()}
243	    />
244	  ),
245	  cell: (cellContext) => (
246	    <CustomRangedSelectionCheckbox
247	      size="l"
248	      checked={cellContext.row.getIsSelected()}
249	      disabled={!cellContext.row.getCanSelect()}
250	      indeterminate={cellContext.row.getIsSomeSelected()}
251	      cellContext={cellContext}
252	    />
253	  ),
254	  size: 41,
255	  maxSize: 41,
256	  minSize: 41,
257	  enableResizing: false,
258	  enableSorting: false,
259	};
260	
261	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
262	  customSelectionColumn as ColumnDef<Person>,
263	  // ...other columns
264	];
265	
266	const data: Person[] = [
267	  /* ... */
268	];
269	
270	const RowRangedSelectionExample = () => {
271	  const [rowSelection, setRowSelection] = useState<RowSelectionState>({});
272	
273	  const table = useTable({
274	    columns,
275	    data,
276	    enableRowSelection: true,
277	    enableMultiRowSelection: true,
278	    onRowSelectionChange: setRowSelection,
279	    state: {
280	      rowSelection,
281	    },
282	  });
283	
284	  return <Table table={table} />;
285	};
286	```
287	
288	There is also a `RangedSelectionCheckbox` component, which internally uses the hook and accepts a `CellContext` instance as a prop. This component provides a shorthand for adding ranged selection functionality to custom selection columns.
289	
290	```tsx
291	import type {ColumnDef} from '@gravity-ui/table/tanstack';
292	import {RangedSelectionCheckbox, SelectionCheckbox} from '@gravity-ui/table';
293	
294	export const selectionColumn: ColumnDef<unknown> = {
295	  id: '_select',
296	  header: ({table}) => (
297	    <SelectionCheckbox
298	      checked={table.getIsAllRowsSelected()}
299	      disabled={!table.options.enableRowSelection}
300	      indeterminate={table.getIsSomeRowsSelected()}
301	      onChange={table.getToggleAllRowsSelectedHandler()}
302	    />
303	  ),
304	  cell: (cellContext) => (
305	    <RangedSelectionCheckbox
306	      checked={cellContext.row.getIsSelected()}
307	      disabled={!cellContext.row.getCanSelect()}
308	      indeterminate={cellContext.row.getIsSomeSelected()}
309	      cellContext={cellContext}
310	    />
311	  ),
312	  meta: {
313	    hideInSettings: true,
314	  },
315	  size: 32,
316	  minSize: 32,
317	};
318	```
319	
320	By default, the selection column generated with `selectionColumn` includes ranged selection functionality.
321	
322	```tsx
323	import {selectionColumn} from '@gravity-ui/table';
324	import type {ColumnDef} from '@gravity-ui/table/tanstack';
325	
326	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
327	  selectionColumn as ColumnDef<Person>,
328	  // ...other columns
329	];
330	```
331	
332	**Note**: If the table contains nested rows, range selection will not work. At the moment, this is considered undefined behavior.
333	
334	#### Sorting
335	
336	Learn about the column properties in the react-table [docs](https://tanstack.com/table/v8/docs/guide/sorting)
337	
338	```tsx
339	import type {SortingState} from '@gravity-ui/table/tanstack';
340	
341	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
342	  /* ... */
343	];
344	
345	const data: Person[] = [
346	  /* ... */
347	];
348	
349	const SortingExample = () => {
350	  const [sorting, setSorting] = React.useState<SortingState>([]);
351	
352	  // Your column MUST have accessorFn for sorting to be enabled
353	
354	  const table = useTable({
355	    columns,
356	    data,
357	    enableSorting: true,
358	    getRowId: (item) => item.id,
359	    onSortingChange: setSorting,
360	    state: {
361	      sorting,
362	    },
363	  });
364	
365	  return <Table table={table} />;
366	};
367	```
368	
369	If you want to sort the elements manually pass `manualSorting` property:
370	
371	```tsx
372	const table = useTable({
373	  // ...
374	  manualSorting: true,
375	});
376	```
377	
378	#### Grouping
379	
380	```tsx
381	import type {ExpandedState, Row} from '@gravity-ui/table/tanstack';
382	
383	interface Person {
384	  id: string;
385	  name: string;
386	  age: number;
387	}
388	
389	interface PersonGroup {
390	  id: string;
391	  name: string;
392	  items: Person[];
393	}
394	
395	type Item = PersonGroup | Person;
396	
397	const columns: ColumnDef<Item>[] = [
398	  {accessorKey: 'name', header: 'Name', size: 200},
399	  {accessorKey: 'age', header: 'Age', size: 100},
400	];
401	
402	const data: Item[] = [
403	  {
404	    id: 'friends',
405	    name: 'Friends',
406	    items: [
407	      {id: 'nick', name: 'Nick', age: 25},
408	      {id: 'tom', name: 'Tom', age: 21},
409	    ],
410	  },
411	  {
412	    id: 'relatives',
413	    name: 'Relatives',
414	    items: [
415	      {id: 'john', name: 'John', age: 23},
416	      {id: 'michael', name: 'Michael', age: 27},
417	    ],
418	  },
419	];
420	
421	const getGroupTitle = (row: Row<Item>) => row.getValue<string>('name');
422	
423	const GroupingExample = () => {
424	  const [expanded, setExpanded] = React.useState<ExpandedState>({});
425	
426	  const table = useTable({
427	    columns,
428	    data,
429	    enableExpanding: true,
430	    getSubRows: (item) => ('items' in item ? item.items : undefined),
431	    onExpandedChange: setExpanded,
432	    state: {
433	      expanded,
434	    },
435	  });
436	
437	  return <Table table={table} getGroupTitle={getGroupTitle} />;
438	};
439	```
440	
441	To use grouping with selection, use `useRowSelectionFixedHandler` hook. Without it parent row checkbox state will be wrong. https://github.com/TanStack/table/issues/4878
442	
443	To enable nesting styles, pass `withNestingStyles = true` in the column configuration.
444	
445	Nesting indicators can be disabled by passing `showTreeDepthIndicators = false`.
446	
447	To add a control for expanding/collapsing rows, wrap the cell content with the `TreeExpandableCell` component or with your similar custom component:
448	
449	```tsx
450	import {TreeExpandableCell} from '@gravity-ui/table';
451	
452	const columns: ColumnDef<Item>[] = [
453	  {
454	    accessorKey: 'name',
455	    header: 'Name',
456	    size: 200,
457	    showTreeDepthIndicators: false,
458	    withNestingStyles: true,
459	    cell: ({row, info}) => (
460	      <TreeExpandableCell row={row}>{info.getValue<string>()}</TreeExpandableCell>
461	    ),
462	  },
463	  // ...other columns
464	];
465	```
466	
467	#### Reordering
468	
469	```tsx
470	import type {ReorderingProviderProps} from '@gravity-ui/table';
471	import {dragHandleColumn, ReorderingProvider} from '@gravity-ui/table';
472	
473	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
474	  dragHandleColumn,
475	  // ...other columns
476	];
477	
478	const data: Person[] = [
479	  /* ... */
480	];
481	
482	const ReorderingExample = () => {
483	  const table = useTable({
484	    columns,
485	    data,
486	    getRowId: (item) => item.id,
487	  });
488	
489	  const handleReorder = React.useCallback<
490	    NonNullable<ReorderingProviderProps<Person>['onReorder']>
491	  >(
492	    ({
493	      draggedItemKey,
494	      targetItemKey,
495	      baseItemKey,
496	      baseNextItemKey,
497	      enableNesting,
498	      nextChild,
499	      pullFromParent,
500	    }) => {
501	      // ...
502	    },
503	    [],
504	  );
505	
506	  return (
507	    <ReorderingProvider table={table} onReorder={handleReorder}>
508	      <Table table={table} />
509	    </ReorderingProvider>
510	  );
511	};
512	```
513	
514	#### Reordering without a drag handle
515	
516	Set `dragWithoutHandle` to use the whole row as the drag activator and omit
517	`dragHandleColumn` from the column definitions:
518	
519	```tsx
520	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
521	  {accessorKey: 'name', header: 'Name'},
522	  {accessorKey: 'age', header: 'Age'},
523	];
524	
525	return (
526	  <ReorderingProvider table={table} dragWithoutHandle onReorder={handleReorder}>
527	    <Table table={table} />
528	  </ReorderingProvider>
529	);
530	```
531	
532	The pointer must move by 8 pixels before dragging starts, so regular row and control clicks keep
533	working. To exclude a custom part of a row from starting a drag, call `preventDefault()` in its
534	`onPointerDown` handler.
535	
536	`ReorderingProvider` enables dnd-kit's vertical auto-scroll by default. Pass `autoScroll={false}`
537	when the application supplies its own drag auto-scroll implementation; running both at once can
538	produce competing scroll writes.
539	
540	Custom drag handles should read `attributes`, `listeners`, and `setActivatorNodeRef` from
541	`DraggableRowContext` and attach them to the handle element. This reuses the row's DnD
542	registration. Do not call `useSortable` again with the same row id: a handle mounted later
543	by virtualization would replace the row's registered DOM node.
544	
545	#### Keyboard reordering and accessibility
546	
547	`ReorderingProvider` supports keyboard row dragging.
548	Focus a drag handle, press Space or Enter to pick up the row, use the arrow keys to move it, and press
549	Space or Enter to drop it. Escape cancels the move.
550	Keyboard dragging applies only to rows; keyboard interactions with column headers remain unchanged.
551	
552	Use `accessibility` to customize dnd-kit's screen reader instructions, announcements, announcement
553	container, and focus restoration for both keyboard and pointer dragging.
554	When row and column providers are nested, they share the same DnD context and accessibility settings;
555	provider order does not matter.
556	
557	```tsx
558	<ReorderingProvider
559	  table={table}
560	  onReorder={handleReorder}
561	  accessibility={{
562	    screenReaderInstructions: {
563	      draggable:
564	        'Press Space to pick up a row, arrow keys to move, Enter to drop, or Escape to cancel.',
565	    },
566	  }}
567	>
568	  <Table table={table} />
569	</ReorderingProvider>
570	```
571	
572	#### Column reordering
573	
574	Wrap the table with `ColumnReorderingProvider` to enable drag-and-drop reordering of columns by their headers.
575	
576	```tsx
577	import {ColumnReorderingProvider} from '@gravity-ui/table';
578	
579	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
580	  {accessorKey: 'name', header: 'Name', size: 100},
581	  {accessorKey: 'age', header: 'Age', size: 100},
582	];
583	
584	const ColumnReorderingExample = () => {
585	  const table = useTable({
586	    columns,
587	    data,
588	    getRowId: (item) => item.id,
589	  });
590	
591	  return (
592	    <ColumnReorderingProvider table={table}>
593	      <Table table={table} />
594	    </ColumnReorderingProvider>
595	  );
596	};
597	```
598	
599	### Row and column reordering together
600	
601	Nest `ColumnReorderingProvider` and `ReorderingProvider` to enable both drag axes at once. The order of providers does not matter — they share a single dnd-kit context internally.
602	
603	```tsx
604	import type {ColumnReorderingProviderProps, ReorderingProviderProps} from '@gravity-ui/table';
605	import {ColumnReorderingProvider, ReorderingProvider, dragHandleColumn} from '@gravity-ui/table';
606	
607	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
608	  dragHandleColumn,
609	  {accessorKey: 'name', header: 'Name'},
610	  {accessorKey: 'age', header: 'Age'},
611	];
612	
613	const CombinedReorderingExample = () => {
614	  const [data, setData] = React.useState(initialData);
615	  const [columnOrder, setColumnOrder] = React.useState<string[]>([]);
616	
617	  const table = useTable({
618	    columns,
619	    data,
620	    getRowId: (item) => item.id,
621	    state: {columnOrder},
622	    onColumnOrderChange: setColumnOrder,
623	  });
624	
625	  const handleRowReorder = React.useCallback<
626	    NonNullable<ReorderingProviderProps<Person>['onReorder']>
627	  >(({draggedItemKey, baseItemKey}) => {
628	    // update data array
629	  }, []);
630	
631	  const handleColumnReorder = React.useCallback<
632	    NonNullable<ColumnReorderingProviderProps<Person>['onReorder']>
633	  >(({columnOrder}) => {
634	    setColumnOrder(columnOrder);
635	  }, []);
636	
637	  return (
638	    <ColumnReorderingProvider table={table} onReorder={handleColumnReorder}>
639	      <ReorderingProvider table={table} onReorder={handleRowReorder}>
640	        <Table table={table} />
641	      </ReorderingProvider>
642	    </ColumnReorderingProvider>
643	  );
644	};
645	```
646	
647	If you control `columnOrder` yourself (e.g. to persist it), pass `onReorder` and apply the resulting order:
648	
649	```tsx
650	const [columnOrder, setColumnOrder] = React.useState<string[]>([]);
651	
652	const table = useTable({
653	  columns,
654	  data,
655	  state: {columnOrder},
656	  onColumnOrderChange: setColumnOrder,
657	});
658	
659	return (
660	  <ColumnReorderingProvider
661	    table={table}
662	    onReorder={({columnOrder}) => setColumnOrder(columnOrder)}
663	  >
664	    <Table table={table} />
665	  </ColumnReorderingProvider>
666	);
667	```
668	
669	CSS API:
670	
671	| CSS variable                                 | Default                       | Description                      |
672	| -------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
673	| `--gt-table-reordering-insertion-line-color` | `#4d8bff`                     | Color of the drop insertion line |
674	| `--gt-table-reordering-insertion-line-width` | `2px`                         | Width of the drop insertion line |
675	| `--gt-table-reordering-dragged-opacity`      | `0.4`                         | Opacity of the dragged column    |
676	| `--gt-table-drag-overlay-background`         | `#fff`                        | Drag preview background          |
677	| `--gt-table-drag-overlay-shadow`             | `0 3px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.15)` | Drag preview box-shadow          |
678	| `--gt-table-drag-overlay-border-radius`      | `6px`                         | Drag preview border radius       |
679	
680	To forbid reordering a specific column, set `enableColumnReordering: false` in its column definition. Placeholder (grouped) columns are not draggable. Use `activationDistance` (default `8`) to tune how far the pointer must move before a drag starts, which keeps header clicks (like sorting) working.
681	
682	Pinned columns can be reordered too, but only among themselves: a column can be moved within the left-pinned group, the right-pinned group, or the center (non-pinned) group — it never crosses a pin boundary by dragging.
683	
684	```tsx
685	<ColumnReorderingProvider
686	  table={table}
687	  onReorder={({columnOrder, columnPinning, pinned}) => {
688	    if (pinned) {
689	      setColumnPinning(columnPinning);
690	    } else {
691	      setColumnOrder(columnOrder);
692	    }
693	  }}
694	>
695	  <Table table={table} />
696	</ColumnReorderingProvider>
697	```
698	
699	While dragging:
700	
701	- a floating preview of the column (its header plus the first rows) follows the pointer in a drag overlay;
702	- the dragged column becomes semi-transparent;
703	- a blue insertion line is drawn where the column will be dropped;
704	
705	```tsx
706	<ColumnReorderingProvider
707	  table={table}
708	  autoScroll
709	  dragOverlayRowCount={10}
710	  renderDragOverlay={({columnId}) => <CustomColumnPreview columnId={columnId} />}
711	>
712	  <Table table={table} />
713	</ColumnReorderingProvider>
714	```
715	
716	#### Virtualization
717	
718	Use if you want to use grid container as the scroll element (if you want to use window see window virtualization section). Be sure to set a fixed height on the container; otherwise, virtualization will not work.
719	
720	```tsx
721	import {useRowVirtualizer} from '@gravity-ui/table';
722	
723	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
724	  /* ... */
725	];
726	
727	const data: Person[] = [
728	  /* ... */
729	];
730	
731	const VirtualizationExample = () => {
732	  const table = useTable({
733	    columns,
734	    data,
735	    getRowId: (item) => item.id,
736	  });
737	
738	  const containerRef = React.useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
739	
740	  const rowVirtualizer = useRowVirtualizer({
741	    count: table.getRowModel().rows.length,
742	    estimateSize: () => 20,
743	    overscan: 5,
744	    getScrollElement: () => containerRef.current,
745	  });
746	
747	  return (
748	    <div ref={containerRef} style={{height: '500px', overflow: 'auto'}}>
749	      <Table table={table} rowVirtualizer={rowVirtualizer} />
750	    </div>
751	  );
752	};
753	```
754	
755	For tables that must stay covered during continuous bidirectional scrolling, enable the adaptive
756	direct-DOM mode and use stable semantic keys. The same key must identify a row before and after an
757	immutable reorder or a tree reparent:
758	
759	```tsx
760	import {getColumnAwareRowOverscan} from '@gravity-ui/table';
761	
762	const rows = table.getRowModel().rows;
763	const columnCount = table.getVisibleLeafColumns().length;
764	
765	const getItemKey = React.useCallback(
766	  (index: number) => rows[index]?.id ?? `missing:${index}`,
767	  [rows],
768	);
769	
770	const rowVirtualizer = useRowVirtualizer({
771	  adaptiveFlushSync: true,
772	  count: rows.length,
773	  directDomUpdates: true,
774	  directDomUpdatesMode: 'position',
775	  estimateSize: () => 40,
776	  getItemKey,
777	  getScrollElement: () => containerRef.current,
778	  overscan: getColumnAwareRowOverscan(columnCount),
779	});
780	```
781	
782	`adaptiveFlushSync` keeps a warm mounted range and synchronously fills only an uncovered visible
783	range. `directDomUpdates` lets the virtualizer update row positions and the body size without a
784	React render for every scroll notification. Use `position` for table rows unless transforms are
785	required by the surrounding layout. Keep `getRowId` and `getItemKey` stable, and set `count` from
786	the current flattened row model after expanding, collapsing, reordering, or reparenting rows.
787	An arbitrary custom `rangeExtractor` remains authoritative and disables adaptive window planning.
788	
789	`getColumnAwareRowOverscan(columnCount, options?)` reduces the base row overscan as the number
790	of columns grows. By default, it divides a 240-cell budget by the column count, rounds down,
791	and clamps the result to 4–24 rows. Use `table.getVisibleLeafColumns().length` to exclude hidden
792	columns and include pinned columns. The helper works with both `useRowVirtualizer` and
793	`useWindowRowVirtualizer`; you can still pass an explicit numeric `overscan` instead.
794	
795	Tune the budget and bounds for your cell rendering cost. If your application virtualizes columns,
796	set `renderedColumnLimit` to the maximum number of columns rendered per row, including pinned
797	columns; the helper caps the supplied column count at this value:
798	
799	```tsx
800	const overscan = getColumnAwareRowOverscan(table.getVisibleLeafColumns().length, {
801	  renderedColumnLimit: 16,
802	  cellBudget: 320,
803	  minOverscan: 4,
804	  maxOverscan: 20,
805	});
806	```
807	
808	The result is a base row overscan, not a strict limit on mounted rows or cells. Visible rows are
809	rendered in addition to the overscan, and adaptive scrolling can extend the mounted range.
810	All helper inputs must be non-negative safe integers, and `maxOverscan` must be at least
811	`minOverscan`; invalid values throw a `RangeError`. Zero columns are treated as one for the calculation.
812	
813	`BaseTable.canDeferOffscreenCellContent` is an additional opt-in for very wide adaptive tables.
814	Return `true` only for passive cell content whose delayed mount cannot change geometry, focus,
815	accessibility, or application state. Custom rows, group rows, pinned cells, and interactive or
816	side-effectful content should remain eager.
817	
818	With the default adaptive range extractor, `BaseTable` pins the active dragged row automatically.
819	A custom range extractor is responsible for retaining that row itself. If you use reordering with
820	a non-adaptive virtualizer, keep the same semantic `getItemKey` contract and pass the
821	`rangeExtractor` option:
822	
823	```tsx
824	import {getVirtualRowRangeExtractor} from '@gravity-ui/table';
825	
826	// ...
827	
828	const tableRef = React.useRef<HTMLTableElement>(null);
829	
830	const rowVirtualizer = useRowVirtualizer({
831	  // ...
832	  rangeExtractor: getVirtualRowRangeExtractor(tableRef.current),
833	});
834	
835	return (
836	  <TableWithReordering
837	    ref={tableRef}
838	    table={table}
839	    rowVirtualizer={rowVirtualizer}
840	    onReorder={handleReorder}
841	  />
842	);
843	```
844	
845	#### Window virtualization
846	
847	Use if you want to use window as the scroll element
848	
849	```tsx
850	import {useWindowRowVirtualizer} from '@gravity-ui/table';
851	
852	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
853	  /* ... */
854	];
855	
856	const data: Person[] = [
857	  /* ... */
858	];
859	
860	const WindowVirtualizationExample = () => {
861	  const table = useTable({
862	    columns,
863	    data,
864	    getRowId: (item) => item.id,
865	  });
866	
867	  const bodyRef = React.useRef<HTMLTableSectionElement>(null);
868	
869	  const rowVirtualizer = useWindowRowVirtualizer({
870	    count: table.getRowModel().rows.length,
871	    estimateSize: () => 20,
872	    overscan: 5,
873	    scrollMargin: bodyRef.current?.offsetTop ?? 0,
874	  });
875	
876	  return <Table table={table} rowVirtualizer={rowVirtualizer} bodyRef={bodyRef} />;
877	};
878	```
879	
880	#### Resizing
881	
882	```tsx
883	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
884	  /* ... */
885	];
886	
887	const data: Person[] = [
888	  /* ... */
889	];
890	
891	const ResizingDemo = () => {
892	  const table = useTable({
893	    columns,
894	    data,
895	    enableColumnResizing: true,
896	    columnResizeMode: 'onChange',
897	  });
898	
899	  return <Table table={table} />;
900	};
901	```
902	
903	#### Column settings
904	
905	Set `enableReset` to `true` to show the settings popup's Reset button (hidden by default).
906	It restores column visibility and order from the table's `initialState`. Reset changes
907	the popup draft; press Apply to save it. Without an `initialState`, Reset shows all
908	columns in their definition order.
909	The optional `onSettingsReset` callback receives that restored visibility and column order
910	when Reset is clicked, before the draft is applied.
911	
912	```tsx
913	const columns: ColumnDef<Person>[] = [
914	  // ...other columns
915	  {
916	    id: 'settings_column_id',
917	    header: ({table}) => <TableSettings table={table} />,
918	    meta: {
919	      hideInSettings: false, // Optional. Allows to hide this column from settings popover
920	      titleInSettings: 'ReactNode', // Optional. Overrides header field for settings popover (if you need different content for header and settings popover)
921	    },
922	  }, // or you can use function getSettingsColumn
923	];
924	
925	const data: Person[] = [
926	  /* ... */
927	];
928	
929	const TableSettingsDemo = () => {
930	  const [columnVisibility, onColumnVisibilityChange] = React.useState<VisibilityState>({
931	    // for outside control and initial state
932	    column_id: false, // for hidding by default
933	  });
934	  const [columnOrder, onColumnOrderChange] = React.useState<string[]>([
935	    /* leaf columns ids */
936	  ]); // for outside control and initial state
937	
938	  // Alternative variant to get state, callbacks, and set on setting apply callbacks - using useTableSettings hook:
939	  // const {state, callbacks} = useTableSettings({initialVisibility: {}, initialOrder: []})
940	
941	  const table = useTable({
942	    columns,
943	    data,
944	    state: {
945	      columnVisibility,
946	      columnOrder,
947	    },
948	    onColumnVisibilityChange,
949	    onColumnOrderChange,
950	  });
951	
952	  return <Table table={table} />;
953	};
954	```
955	
956	Learn more about the table and the column resizing properties in the react-table [docs](https://tanstack.com/table/v8/docs/api/features/column-sizing)
957	
958	## Guides
959	
960	- [Migration Guide: From Table (@gravity-ui/uikit) to Table (@gravity-ui/table)](./guides/migration-from-uikit-table/migration-from-uikit-table.md)
961	- [Руководство по миграции с Table (@gravity-ui/uikit) на Table (@gravity-ui/table)](./guides/migration-from-uikit-table/migration-from-uikit-table-ru.md)
962	
963	## Components
964	
965	- [BaseTable](./components/BaseTable.md) — The unstyled, low-level table renderer — renders a useTable instance as raw <table> markup without Gravity UI styling, for full visual control.
966	
967	## Hooks
968	
969	- [useColumnsAutoSize](./hooks/useColumnsAutoSize.md) — A React hook that automatically calculates column widths based on measured content, supporting primitives and React nodes, accessorKey/accessorFn columns, custom cell renderers, and respect for predefined or user-resized widths.

events.content:
The content pane (`gn-aside-header__content`) has `width: calc(100% - aside size)` and `margin-top`, but no explicit height/overflow. The aside itself is `height: 100vh; position: sticky`. So the page scroll is the document scroll by default; the content pane grows with content. For my sticky-header table I want a bounded scroll container: I'll give the orders page root `height: 100vh; display: flex; flex-direction: column; overflow: hidden` with inner container `flex:1; min-height:0; overflow:auto`. Since the content pane is in normal flow at document level, height:100vh works well (document won't scroll because content is exactly viewport height).

Now write the files.

Data: 24 orders, statuses distributed. Russian customer names. Dates Oct–Nov 2026. Totals in ₽.

Formatting total: `new Intl.NumberFormat('ru-RU', {style: 'currency', currency: 'RUB', maximumFractionDigits: 0})`.

Column cell for created date: format `new Intl.DateTimeFormat('ru-RU')`.

Details:
- `getGroupTitle` returns string title; BaseGroupHeader shows count automatically (subRows.length). Nice.
- Sum per group? Keep simple.

Selected count display: `Object.keys(rowSelection).length` — but with nested selection, keys include group ids and leaf ids. useRowSelectionFixedHandler — how does it mark? Probably selects group id + leaf ids (TanStack selects subRows when parent selected). Counting selected ORDERS: count keys that are order ids (not starting with 'group-'). Let me compute: `Object.keys(rowSelection).filter(id => !id.startsWith('group-')).length`. Good enough for the header indicator.

For the sticky header inside scroll container — Table prop `stickyHeader` exists in BaseTable destructuring ✓.

One more check: `Table` accepts `getIsGroupHeaderRow`? Table passes ...props to BaseTable ✓ (TableProps extends BaseTableProps).

Also `SelectionCheckbox` import from '@gravity-ui/table' root ✓ (export * from SelectionCheckbox).

Type for columns: ColumnDef from '@gravity-ui/table/tanstack' — check that subpath's exports include ColumnDef with the extended type? The docs say import ColumnDef from tanstack subpath. The extended ColumnDef with enableColumnReordering is in types/base — maybe the tanstack.d.ts re-exports. Let me check build/esm/tanstack.d.ts.

events.content:
Готово. Дашборд собран на реальных пакетах Gravity UI, выбранных по таблице маршрутизации скилла: `@gravity-ui/navigation` для каркаса и `@gravity-ui/table` (TanStack-based) для таблицы — uikit `Table` для группировки/DnD не предназначен.

**Что установлено** (с учётом uikit 7.43.0 — `navigation@8` требует uikit ^8, поэтому взята совместимая линия):
- `@gravity-ui/navigation@7.1.3`, `@gravity-ui/table@1.25.0` + peer-зависимости (`@dnd-kit/core`, `@dnd-kit/sortable`, `lodash`, `@bem-react/classname`, `@gravity-ui/i18n`)

**Реализация:**
- **`src/App.tsx`** — `AsideHeader` с логотипом и четырьмя разделами (Главная/House, Пользователи/Persons, Заказы/ShoppingCart, Настройки/Gear — все имена иконок сверены с установленным `@gravity-ui/icons`). Сворачивание в иконки — контролируемое `compact`/`onChangeCompact`, встроенная кнопка collapse на краю панели. Контент рендерится через `renderContent`; не-заказные разделы показывают заглушку. Добавлен `configure({lang: 'ru'})`.
- **`src/OrdersPage.tsx`** — таблица заказов:
  - **Выделение строк**: колонка с чекбоксами (`Checkbox` из uikit — `SelectionCheckbox` в этой версии не реэкспортирован из корня пакета, а это тот же компонент), состояние `rowSelection`, обработчик `useRowSelectionFixedHandler` — документированный фикс корректного состояния чекбоксов при вложенных строках (range-выделение с группировкой несовместимо, поэтому не используется).
  - **Перетаскивание колонок**: `ColumnReorderingProvider` + контролируемый `columnOrder`/`onColumnOrderChange` (у selection-колонки `enableColumnReordering: false`).
  - **Группировка по статусу**: данные — группы со `getSubRows`, строки-заголовки групп через `getIsGroupHeaderRow` + `getGroupTitle` (заголовок + счётчик, сворачивание по клику), статус в строках — uikit `Label` с семантическими темами.
  - Sticky-заголовок в собственном скролл-контейнере (`flex: 1; min-height: 0; overflow: auto`), раскладка и рамки на токенах `--g-spacing-*`, `--g-color-line-generic`, `--g-border-radius-l`.
- **`src/ordersData.ts`** — 24 заказа по 5 статусам, метаданные статусов.

**Проверка:** `tsc --noEmit` — чисто, `vite build` — успешно. Тайпчек не покрывает визуальную часть — стоит глазами проверить: светлую/тёмную темы, узкий (~375px) и широкий (~1400px) вьюпорты, а также поведение свёрнутого сайдбара и drag-превью колонок. Запуск: `npm run dev`.
